title: Plural genitive of common -i words
summary: Use -ien with the plural stems in this lesson: bussi (“bus”) → bussien.
objectives: Use -ien with the plural stems in this lesson: bussi (“bus”) → bussien.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A plural genitive refers to more than one person or thing. Its ending belongs to the plural modifier, not necessarily to the thing owned. Here the task is forming the word.
Use -ien with the plural stems in this lesson. Several words that change i in the singular return to an i-based plural form; learn the plural directly.
keyPoints: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.

steps: Keep bussi and add -en: bussi + en = bussien.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.

Use käsi- before -en: käsi + en = käsien. This lesson uses the ordinary modern plural form.

Use vesi- before -en: vesi + en = vesien. Plural vesi can refer to bodies of water.
